logline: A short boy who refuses to let his height end his volleyball dream joins a high school team of misfits and argues his way toward the top of the high school circuit - one match at a time.

renewal.note: The TV series concluded December 2020 after four seasons. Two theatrical films continue the story: Haikyu!! The Dumpster Battle (2024) and Haikyu!! The Movie: Battle of Concepts (announced).

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.7 overall series; 94% on Rotten Tomatoes from 4 critic reviews. Critics praised Production I.G.'s dynamic animation and the show's ability to make volleyball mechanically compelling even to viewers with no prior interest in the sport.

pull_quotes.text: A shonen anime packed in volleyball wrapping - how the tosses and serves and receives got my heart a-poundin'!

seasons.review_body: Season 1 of Haikyu!! debuted April 2014 on Production I.G. and demonstrated what the studio could do with kinetic sport animation. The 25-episode first season covers Karasuno's reformation as a competitive team, establishing the ensemble with efficiency and warmth. Critics scored it 94 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, with reviewers noting the series' core achievement: making volleyball's technical vocabulary legible and dramatic simultaneously. The Shogakukan Manga Award the source material won translated into an adaptation that understood what made the original work. The IMDb score of 8.7 - among the highest for a sports anime - reflects how many viewers arrived with no volleyball interest and left convinced.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.7 overall. Season 2 is widely regarded as the strongest of the multi-episode seasons, with the Spring High Preliminary tournament delivering some of the franchise's most celebrated match sequences.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 aired from October 2015 to March 2016 and raised the stakes with the Inter-High and Spring High Preliminary tournaments. Production I.G. maintained the animation quality across a 25-episode run, and the match against Aoba Johsai stands as the season's defining set piece. Character writing deepened significantly: Kageyama and Hinata's partnership shifts from mutual irritation toward something closer to genuine understanding, while the supporting cast receives material that pays off the investment set up in Season 1. IMDb users keep Season 2’s ranking strong alongside Season 1, placing the sequel among the franchise’s best.
seasons.season_over_season: Expands the tournament scope and deepens the central character dynamics - the Spring High arc justifies the full 25-episode investment.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb audience consistently rates Season 3 as the series' best-scored season. Ten episodes devoted entirely to the Karasuno-Shiratorizawa match, giving each set the full dramatic expansion the stakes warranted.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 is a singular experiment in sports anime pacing: 10 episodes covering a single five-set match between Karasuno and Shiratorizawa. The format pays off. By devoting this kind of screen time to each rotation, each substitution, each tactical adjustment, Production I.G. transformed a volleyball match into something closer to a character study with a ball. Ushijima is the franchise's most formidable opponent precisely because the show allows him to be visibly correct about almost everything except the final result. Audience ratings for Season 3 are the franchise's highest, with episode-level IMDb scores placing the finale as among the best individual episodes in the series.
seasons.season_over_season: A focused 10-episode format that turns a single match into the franchise's most dramatically sustained sequence.

episode_reviews.title: The Halo Around the Moon
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The final episode of the Shiratorizawa match. The fifth set resolution earns every episode of buildup that preceded it, and Production I.G.'s animation in the final rally puts the studio at its competitive peak.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The match-winning point - a moment the show has been building toward across ten episodes of pressure, and which lands with the force of everything that preceded it.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.7 overall. Season 4 covers the national tournament qualifiers in a split-cour format across January-April and October-December 2020. Audience reception remained strong; the Inarizaki match is frequently cited in season reviews as a new franchise highlight.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 (To the Top) aired in two cours across January-April and October-December 2020, covering the Spring High National Tournament. The split-cour format introduced a mid-season hiatus that broke the narrative momentum slightly, but the Inarizaki match in the second cour is among the franchise's most celebrated tournament sequences. Production I.G. updated their visual approach for the national stage, with more dynamic camera placement in the service of a larger-scale competition. The season served as the TV series finale, with the narrative continuing in theatrical films. Audience ratings held at the franchise high, and the Miya twins' introduction added competitive texture to the opposition roster.
seasons.season_over_season: The national-stage upgrade in animation and opposition quality makes Season 4 a worthy finale for the TV run.
